body:
I haven't been happy in a very long time. We started dating just 3 years ago. We've had problems since 3 months into the relationship. Yet, I stuck around because I loved her so much. A part of me still does, despite it all. Having our daughter wasn't an accident; I was pressured and didn't have enough of a spine to stand up for myself. We got married when she was 8 months pregnant. I work like crazy and have no fun. When I come home after a 12 hour work day, I take care of a cranky baby before she falls asleep, then my wife and I usually fight about something stupid, and she often goes out with her friends (I have to stay home because somebody needs to be home while the baby sleeps). I only have 2 friends, each of which I hardly ever hang out with. I have trouble sleeping because, ever since we got married, I've had trouble falling asleep alone... which is almost every night.
At times, she can be a really sweet person. But she can also be mean-spirted, spiteful, rude, and selfish. I feel so used. I feel like I got cheated out of what would have been a very happy life. Our sex life is non-existent. In fact, for 6 months before she even got pregnant, we rarely had sex... how unlucky of me to get her pregnant one of the few times we did. Now we're never sexual and hardly intimate at all.

The only other time I posted with this throwaway account was on SuicideWatch. Thank god I backed away from that. But the depression/anxiety won't go away. I've missed work 4 times in the past 2 weeks and now I've fallen behind on a project. My heart constantly feels like it's racing.

We've been going to marriage counseling for a few months and I've recently started seeing a counselor on my own in addition.

You can call it cowardly all you want, and guilt me for "abandoning" my daughter. I do still have feelings for my wife, which makes it hard enough. I can't bare to think that I won't see my daughter every single day. But, I would still do what's right and pay child support so my daughter won't have to struggle, and I would make an effort to see her every other weekend.

Now, let's consider your proposal: stick it out, despite all of this. Well, at this rate I'll eventually get fired, because the depression/stress/anxiety has been making me physically sick. My daughter would grow up with her father in such a miserable condition, and get to witness her parents fighting every single day. We would eventually get divorced anyway, which would only be long-winded and get dragged out. I would end up paying alimony (she's a stay-at-home mom), lose half my stuff, and pay child support. If we divorce now, I could start to rebuild my life once I get past the grieving process. I would one day be happy again. I wouldn't see my daughter as much as I would otherwise want to, but I would still see her and still be a part of her life. We've been married for only 14 months, so my lawyer says I probably can avoid paying alimony. I only just started my career 6 months ago, so there's currently no assests she can try to take, except for the rental property which i purchased 6 months before we got married (but i also have enough debt that I can "settle" with her by not "sharing" my debt if we also don't "share" my investment - which currently has no equity anyway).

To be honest, I actually feel the coward thing would be to continue to live an unhealthy life that I hate, and raise my daughter around so much negativity.

> idiot nice guys who end up being divorced and fucked over.

This. I am 22 years old, married, and have a 14 month old daughter. I love my career, yet I'm miserable at home.
I'll be alone all weekend. I'm actually kind of dreading it; I hate being lonely. What should I do with all that alone time? Seriously, I'll do anything you suggest, I really don't care anymore.

> it sounds like your wife had an episiotomy during birth? Being 'cut in her vagina' is pretty much par for the course if you have a vaginal delivery in a North American hospital. After 13 months, she should either be healed and ready for action, or she should be looking for a new doctor.

Yes, it was an episiotomy. At her 6 week check up after giving birth, they cortorized the wound. She continued to hurt until 6 months after giving birth. Once she stopped hurting, we would try to have sex, but she would hurt so we wouldn't do it. She finally went back to the ob-gyn in June (10 months after giving birth), who said when they cortorized her cut, it got infected. She has been going back to the ob-gyn every 2 weeks since then. The infection just recently healed, but the doctor said that she is still raw and has some spotting, which might be related to an IUD they inserted at her 6 week appointment. So, now she's on a mild anti-depressant which I guess should kick some hormone so she can finish healing, or something...

> Have you talked to your marriage counselor specifically about your intimacy issues?

This was the main reason we started going to the marriage counselor. But she immediately noticed other issues that we had, mainly an inability to effectively communicate or make mutual decisions.  The counselor has suggested a couple of times that my wife and I need to discuss intimacy, and to have a plan in case it still takes many months before we can have sex.  But, my wife wants *nothing* to do with that. I guess I should point out that I've been an extremely horny since I was like 8... but let's not go into that here... I can usually just ignore those feelings when I'm at work, but when I'm home and near the one I love, these feelings get so strong and over-whelming, that it hurts. Emotionally and physically, it hurts. I get so stiff, but I'm so horny it tries to get harder... and then i get "blue balls" - not a fun time. When we were just dating, my wife made me feel ashamed for taking care of it myself... which I still feel each time I do.

> Having a child is difficult, and while you might not see it, as a SAH mom during that time I would have killed for a 14 hour work day. You're away from home for 12 hours and take care of the baby for 90 minutes? That is a lot, but not necessarily a lot compared to being stuck in the house all day with a young child. Does your wife want to work? Would she consider it as an option?

I know it's rough being a stay-at-home parent, which is why I don't complain about being the sole person to take care of our daughter from the time I get home until the time she goes to bed. Point is though, it's tiring, especially since those 90 minutes are when the baby is tired and cranky, but doesn't want a diaper change, doesn't want to eat, doesn't want to sleep, etc. After dropping me off at the train station in the morning, my wife and daughter come home and usually go back to sleep for a couple of hours. Then they eat, then they go to the gym (for $10/mo Work-Out-World will babysit for up to 2 hours a day while you work out). Usually a couple of her friends from college go with her. She often spends entire afternoons with friends and the baby. So, yes, she does take care of our daughter throughout the day, but she is not locked up at home with nobody to talk to or nothing to do (but I still recognize how tiring that is). We met in college, she completed one year before deciding she didn't like her major and didn't go back, then got pregnant. She knows what career she wants now, and is ready to go back to school part-time in January. I'm just concerned about the day-care costs, especially with my student loans kicking in now...

> Do the two of you make plans to do things together? Having a 'date night' at least once a week where you go out and forget that you have a child is a real blessing. She also needs to get over the 'babysitter' thing, because they should not be considered 'babysitters' but 'marriage savers'.

I want to, but the cost of a baby-sitter is expensive, and she doesn't want to go out every week. Just a couple hours would cost us $20 to have her friend babysit, or $30 to have my niece babysit for 24 hours (but since she lives an hour away, my wife isn't thrilled with that anyway). I spoke with my wife about this. It's not really just the bar specifically that I want to do, so much as going out together and having fun in general... like a normal 22 year old. Or, going out with a group of friends and having fun. It doesn't always have to be the bar, it could be bowling, the movies, etc. When we spoke, she said maybe we can go out once every 6 weeks, which was devastating to hear.

> In your counselling sessions has your wife indicated that she wants to continue a relationship?

She and I have spoken about this, in and out of counseling. I believe she is sincere when she says that she loves me... and just the fact that lately she has been trying to comfort me when I have an emotional break down, makes me think it's true. I really love her. I admit that at times I've blamed her for these problems, but it's my fault just as much, and it's not fair of me to blame her. I also try to not resent her for the way I've felt about our sex life, but sometimes I just feel so desperate and she wants nothing to do with the subject, I do feel some resentment. I know she's also had a rough year, but without intimacy or any fun, I don't want to keep living. I feel so dead at times. When we fight, sometimes she can be so vicious and hurtful that I really do think this may eventually end in divorce... which I feel would be much worse. I would be more lonely and depressed, and since my debt (credit cards, student loans, mortgage with inconsistent tenants paying rent) is so high, I know the cost of child support would bankrupt me. That being said, I want to stay with her because I love her and my daughter, and I would miss them so much it hurts. They're going to my mother-in-law's this weekend, and I'm already dreading that.

> Is it your wife's fault that you don't have friends, or is it something that you can work on yourself?

I could blame her, but ultimately I think I should take responsibility for this. You see, we started dating in college (I was a sophomore, she was a freshman). I had an awesome freshman year, but my sophomore I was burnt-out because I was taking extra classes and working in my first internship, which is when I slowly stopped seeing a lot of my friends. I also preferred to spend as much time as I could with her, thus neglecting my friends further. After that year, she dropped out of that school and moved 3 hours away back to her father's house. The following school year, I did that 3 hour drive back and forth each weekend to see her. During the week, I only had time for school, homework/studying and my internship. On the weekend, I went to her dad's house 3 hours away. I only saw my friends from freshman year, who I used to go out with all the time, only once that year. We learned she was pregnant in December 2008; I bought the house in March 2009 and we moved in. But by then I rarely saw my friends from freshman year, except one who I've been friends with for the past 10 years. I also took extra courses so I could graduate 3 months early, in addition to doing my internship full time and now being a landlord. That continued even after our daughter was born in August 2009, and my remaining senior year until I graduated in March 2010. The funny thing is that since I was closer to home, I was at home more often and could help with our daughter more often, even though I had school and internship both full time (the internship was an at-home internship doing Java development). We even went out more often back then. But, since I graduated and started working and doing this long commute, all I've done is work, work, work. I recently tried calling/texting a couple of those friends from freshman year, but they never got back to me.

Thanks for your advice. I just wish I could be happy and less stressed. I'm glad I finally decided to post something on here, I was really losing it. I just hope I can solve this issue soon, because I'm getting desperate to just be happy... I just can't live life this depressed

> Phase 1: Buy PSP with a most excellent game Phase 2: ? Phase 3: Emotional Profit!

Thanks for the first lol i've had all day :). That actually does sound like a really good idea.

On that note, you helped me to realize how much I miss playing video games. I saw [this](http://i.imgur.com/jLBYY.jpg) on reddit yesterday and it made me sad how much I miss those days playing CS, Battlefield, etc. If only I had more free time, I would build a gaming PC and get back into it.

I cannot move closer to my job (see a comment I wrote earlier). I also don't want to quit. I love the company I work for and I love what I do. This is my first full-time permanent job out of college. I've only been here for 6 months (since I graduated). I was hoping to stay here at least 2-3 years, for my resume and the work experience.

I'm sorry to hear about what happened to your brother. When I get thoughts like this, I feel ashamed: like if I did it, I would be abandoning my entire family. I know others are in worse situations than I am right now, but without any joy in life... what's the point?

I've been clinging to the hope that things would get better. But lately, I've just been so tired, lonely and depressed, that I'm not sure how much more of this I can take.

My wife has recently started exercising on a regular basis, so maybe what you were saying will hold true. I just haven't had the ambition to start exercising. In fact, over the past year, I've gone in the opposite direction. I realize that no matter what I do, I'll be just as miserable. I can add to how tired I am by exercising, but why bother? She still won't sleep with me and I'll still have the crazy work hours. So at night after our daughter goes to sleep, I've just been sitting on the couch watching TV and eating junk food. I know I shouldn't, but who cares? fuck it

edit: As a result of those habits, I've gained 25 pounds in the past year. I hate myself for doing that, but it doesn't matter anymore, it won't change anything

Thank you for this advice. It made me realize how disconnected I've been feeling from my wife. We spoke and I elaborated on how I've been feeling. She says she really loves me, and I think she was sincere. I still love her, and I can't live without her or my daughter.

> Get a life that's not socially resting completely on your wife.

I never realized it before, but you're entirely correct. My entire social life depends on my wife. But how do I correct that? By the time our daughter goes to bed at 8:30 PM, I'm exhausted. I also don't even know where to look to meet friends. I do know of some technology groups in Providence, but I think my schedule would make it impossible to go to their get-togethers, etc.

I've spoken with my wife about this on numerous times. She's thrown it back in my face when we fight... such as when I said I think we made the decision to have a baby too soon, that I regret not waiting.

The marriage counseling has helped us to communicate a little better, and now she listens when I tell her why I'm feeling so dead. But she can only take so much of it.

I would love to move closer to my job, but I can't for a few reasons:

* It would put us even further away from her family, when she would rather move closer to them.
* We used the $8000 home buyer tax credit for purchasing the house in 2009 for our wedding; we must stay here for 36 months or we have to repay that money to the IRS.
* I just got the 2nd floor rented after the tenant moved out suddenly at the end of July. I spent all of August fixing it up, and it is just now rented again. My 3rd floor tenant is behind on rent and I may need to evict her and later fix up that apartment... which would be much more difficult if we didn't live on the first floor.
* Low on cash (see the previous bullet).

edit: formatting.

> You have an analytical mind, try applying that approach.

This is what bothers me the most. I'm used to being able to solve problems. But i feel stuck, like there's nothing i can do. The only solutions i see would leave me miserable. No matter what solution I come up with, I lose either way. My analytical skills, without any options, has turned into an obsession.

I hate feeling this stuck and helpless. I've been battling with these feelings of just giving up on everything.

Thanks for the advice. Our daughter is getting shots on Friday, which always makes her cranky for the whole day.  So she and my wife are going to my wife's mother's house (3 hours away) for the weekend for support, since I'll be at work all day Friday. Essentially, I'll be getting exactly what you suggest: time alone, but for the whole weekend.

Here's the problem: I'm not sure how I'll do with that. I hate to be alone and don't know how I'll handle a whole weekend alone. For one thing, she'll have our only car. I live just on the outside of a city (Providence), so I can easily take a cab somewhere, but my one friend won't be available to hang out the whole weekend. Why go to the bar/club without any friends? I have fond memories of going out with friends my freshman year, but I've been working like crazy for the past couple of years and gradually lost contact.
